metadata.note: Command teardown of ./art scenes and its aliases (scenes, scene, scene-search) — all three collapse into the same case branch in the top-level art dispatcher and exec runtime/scripts/scene_search.py. The middle body walks the 620-entry scene index built by build_scene_index.py, the four ranking rules (id > synonym > haystack, with IDF re-weighting for rare words), the --check anti-slate test, the --undocumented backfill list, and the automatic TEMPLATE-MISSES.md logging that catches a punt in flight. Falsifiability beat: the string 'yak shaving trombone' truly misses (exit 1) and the tool prints 'a miss is a PUNT, do not slate it.' All demo outputs in demo/RUN-LOG.txt are verbatim from this workspace against the isolated toolkit's scenes.json (620 renderable compositions after ClaudeCodeBeat916 was registered here for the portrait companion). Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. No paid API, no upload, no network calls. episode.source_sha256 4759b441d3d6c9faee523870e99fa26482fb28ecaa7cbf9a19b43c1680651a56.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI cold open. Ask lands answered; narration introduces Liam in for Bear.
beats.narration_text: Namaste, this is Liam, in for Bear. There are six hundred and twenty renderable compositions in Brutalist. Nobody remembers them. So when you need a visual for a beat, the first move is not to author one. It is to search. Art scenes is the library-first check that stops a beat from being slated while a purpose-built component sits unused two directories away.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM — the ranking. Three trust tiers, then IDF re-weighting so rare words win.
beats.narration_text: The ranker has one job: put the right lead at the top. Three trust tiers. An id hit is worth three points. A synonym hit is worth two. A hit anywhere else in the haystack — the description, the folder, the props — is worth one. Then it re-weights by inverse document frequency. That means a rare word like sankey outranks a common word like flow, so 'sankey flow' finds FinanceSankey and not every SourceFlow in the set. And a derived-only entry loses half a point, so a scene that actually describes itself outranks a guessed one.

props.title: scene_search.py — score()  (the ranker)
props.code:
def score(s):
    hay = hay_of(s)                # desc + when + folder + group + props
    n = 0
    for t in terms:
        if t in s['id'].lower():   n += 3 * weight(t)  # id      = high trust
        elif t in s['synonyms']:   n += 2 * weight(t)  # synonym = medium trust
        elif t in hay:             n += 1 * weight(t)  # haystack = low trust
    if s.get('desc_source') == 'derived':
        n -= 0.5                   # a described scene beats a guessed one.
    return n

# weight(t): rare word wins.
#   df <= 12 -> 2.0     df <= 60 -> 1.5     else -> 1.0
#
#   'sankey flow'      -> FinanceSankey  (not every SourceFlow in the set)
#   'bar chart'        -> BarChart       (id-hit outweighs every 'chart' entry)

beats.role_note: WORKED EXAMPLE — verbatim output of ./art scenes 'sankey flow' from this workspace.
beats.narration_text: Here is the shape on a real query. Dot slash art scenes quote sankey flow quote. Five candidates. Top of the list is FinanceSankey, scoring eight point five, because sankey is a rare word and it is right there in the id. The three source-flow scenes tie for second at four point five — same common word, spread across a bigger haystack. Every hit shows the id, the aspect ratio, the folder it lives under, and the props you can pass. That is enough to decide without opening a single file.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — the miss. The tool exits 1, prints a punt instruction, and appends to TEMPLATE-MISSES.md.
beats.narration_text: And here is what a real miss looks like. Yak shaving trombone. No scene matches. The tool does not silently return empty. It exits with status one. It prints an instruction: that is a PUNT — do not slate it, design the component, add it to the library. And it does one more thing that nothing else in the toolkit does. It writes the miss to TEMPLATE-MISSES.md with today's date, so the punt ledger does not depend on your discipline. A miss is a design card, filed automatically the moment it happens.
